# Generated MCP inventory

The tool list depends on configured integrations and provider credentials;
there is no single fixed tool count. Each fixture below is generated from
the real schema factories with fake readiness facts.

## Always available (core) (8 tools)

### `triss_chat`

Bare prompt through the configured provider runtime — no corpus or retrieval.

Input properties:

- `provider` — string; one of: openai-compatible, zai, opencode-zen, opencode-go, moonshot, kimi-for-coding. Canonical provider id
- `model` — string. Model id: <canonical-provider>/<native-id> selector, or a bare native id resolved against provider or the effective default provider; conflicting provider selections are rejected
- `engine` — string; one of: direct, opencode, opencode2, omp, crush. Execution engine
- `protect_credentials` — boolean. Use the parent-owned credential proxy for the model projection. A selected protected route fails closed before any credential-bearing spawn when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start; there is no automatic downgrade to raw.
- `effort` — string; one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Reasoning effort
- `prompt` — string (required). Prompt to send
- `system` — string. Optional system prompt / persona
- `max_tokens` — integer. Token budget (default 4096)

- `spec` — string (required). What to write (free-form description)
- `target` — string. Output file path (optional). When set, Triss writes the file.

### `triss_coder_run`

Delegate an implementation task to a coding agent through the configured provider runtime. OpenCode, OpenCode2, OMP, and Crush engine projections are supported. Returns a JSON envelope: {engine, engine_version, session_id, exit_reason, final_text, files_changed, diff_stat, worktree, usage, warnings}. The envelope's `usage` carries the canonical schema_version: 2 shape: `usage.tokens` (input_uncached, cache_read, cache_write, output_visible, reasoning, plus totals) and `usage.cost` (total_usd, source, complete), where an unreported class is `null` rather than `0`; `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` remain as deprecated aliases. OpenCode/OpenCode2 runs use best_effort_raw credential handling — the selected raw provider credential may be read by same-UID engine code, plugins, tools, or shell commands; pass protect_credentials:true for the parent-owned credential proxy with strict executable-surface gates. For compatibility, protectCredentials:true is also accepted on triss_coder_run and is merged safely with protect_credentials. This tool's timeout defaults to 1500s (25 min) since coding runs over MCP are expected to be long; override per call via the `timeout` arg. For runs that may exceed that, use `triss coder run` on the CLI (optionally backgrounded).

Input properties:

- `prompt` — string (required). The task for the coding agent
- `engine` — string; one of: opencode, opencode2, crush, omp. Coding engine (default: opencode V1; opencode2 is the V2 beta; omp uses the pinned Oh My Pi headless adapter; crush is the provider-neutral single-envelope engine; or TRISS_CODER_ENGINE)
- `session` — string. Named session slug for the selected engine; storage and resume compatibility are engine-specific
- `continue` — boolean. Continue a prior session using the resolved engine's supported continuation semantics
- `agent` — string. agent template to use (V1 default: coder; opencode2 beta uses its built-in primary agent unless set)
- `provider` — string; one of: openai-compatible, zai, opencode-zen, opencode-go, moonshot, kimi-for-coding. Canonical provider id
- `model` — string. Model id: <canonical-provider>/<native-id> selector, or a bare native id resolved against provider or the effective default provider; conflicting provider selections are rejected
- `effort` — string; one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Reasoning effort
- `isolate` — boolean. Run in a disposable git worktree under .triss/wt/<slug> (opencode defaults to isolate-OFF; crush defaults to isolate-ON — crush 0.1.3's permissions.run config is inert, so the worktree is its reliable safety layer)
- `allowBestEffortCallerWorktree` — boolean. Explicit opt-in (default FALSE) for caller-worktree execution fallback when isolation cannot be established (without it, such a run fails before spawn with TRISS_CODER_ISOLATION_ENFORCEMENT_REQUIRED; with it, warns TRISS_CODER_ISOLATION_DOWNGRADED and runs as best_effort_caller_worktree).
- `allow_best_effort_caller_worktree` — boolean. Snake-case alias of allowBestEffortCallerWorktree (the handler already accepts it; declared so schema-filtering clients forward it).
- `protectCredentials` — boolean. Deprecated camelCase spelling retained for existing triss_coder_run clients. Use protect_credentials for new calls; both spellings merge as a tri-state — an explicit boolean survives verbatim.
- `protect_credentials` — boolean. Use the parent-owned credential proxy and strict executable-surface gates. Tri-state boolean: absent keeps the engine default (crush: protected), true enables the proxy, an explicit false runs with the selected raw credential and overrides a persisted protection choice. A selected protected route fails closed before any credential-bearing spawn when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start; there is no automatic downgrade to raw.
- `cwd` — string. Working directory (ignored with isolate; sandboxed under MCP)
- `timeout` — number. Seconds before the engine is killed (default 1500 over MCP)

### `triss_coder_status`

Show coding-agent setup: canonical provider credential readiness, default engine, engine versions/install state, configured engine files, and active isolation worktrees.

### `triss_coder_result_list`

List retained coder result artifacts (bounded projection: run_id, engine, session_slug, published_at, state). Never lists persistent sessions.

### `triss_coder_result_clean`

Remove ONLY a validated retained result artifact by its run-id (run-<32 lowercase hex>). Never removes a persistent session selected by a slug.

Input properties:

- `run_id` — string (required). run-id of the retained result to remove

### `triss_coder_run`

Delegate an implementation task to a coding agent through the configured provider runtime. OpenCode, OpenCode2, OMP, and Crush engine projections are supported. Returns a JSON envelope: {engine, engine_version, session_id, exit_reason, final_text, files_changed, diff_stat, worktree, usage, warnings}. The envelope's `usage` carries the canonical schema_version: 2 shape: `usage.tokens` (input_uncached, cache_read, cache_write, output_visible, reasoning, plus totals) and `usage.cost` (total_usd, source, complete), where an unreported class is `null` rather than `0`; `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` remain as deprecated aliases. OpenCode/OpenCode2 runs use best_effort_raw credential handling — the selected raw provider credential may be read by same-UID engine code, plugins, tools, or shell commands; pass protect_credentials:true for the parent-owned credential proxy with strict executable-surface gates. For compatibility, protectCredentials:true is also accepted on triss_coder_run and is merged safely with protect_credentials. This tool's timeout defaults to 1500s (25 min) since coding runs over MCP are expected to be long; override per call via the `timeout` arg. For runs that may exceed that, use `triss coder run` on the CLI (optionally backgrounded).

Input properties:

- `prompt` — string (required). The task for the coding agent
- `engine` — string; one of: opencode, opencode2, crush, omp. Coding engine (default: opencode V1; opencode2 is the V2 beta; omp uses the pinned Oh My Pi headless adapter; crush is the provider-neutral single-envelope engine; or TRISS_CODER_ENGINE)
- `session` — string. Named session slug for the selected engine; storage and resume compatibility are engine-specific
- `continue` — boolean. Continue a prior session using the resolved engine's supported continuation semantics
- `agent` — string. agent template to use (V1 default: coder; opencode2 beta uses its built-in primary agent unless set)
- `provider` — string; one of: openai-compatible, zai, opencode-zen, opencode-go, moonshot, kimi-for-coding. Canonical provider id
- `model` — string. Model id: <canonical-provider>/<native-id> selector, or a bare native id resolved against provider or the effective default provider; conflicting provider selections are rejected
- `effort` — string; one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Reasoning effort
- `isolate` — boolean. Run in a disposable git worktree under .triss/wt/<slug> (opencode defaults to isolate-OFF; crush defaults to isolate-ON — crush 0.1.3's permissions.run config is inert, so the worktree is its reliable safety layer)
- `allowBestEffortCallerWorktree` — boolean. Explicit opt-in (default FALSE) for caller-worktree execution fallback when isolation cannot be established (without it, such a run fails before spawn with TRISS_CODER_ISOLATION_ENFORCEMENT_REQUIRED; with it, warns TRISS_CODER_ISOLATION_DOWNGRADED and runs as best_effort_caller_worktree).
- `allow_best_effort_caller_worktree` — boolean. Snake-case alias of allowBestEffortCallerWorktree (the handler already accepts it; declared so schema-filtering clients forward it).
- `protectCredentials` — boolean. Deprecated camelCase spelling retained for existing triss_coder_run clients. Use protect_credentials for new calls; both spellings merge as a tri-state — an explicit boolean survives verbatim.
- `protect_credentials` — boolean. Use the parent-owned credential proxy and strict executable-surface gates. Tri-state boolean: absent keeps the engine default (crush: protected), true enables the proxy, an explicit false runs with the selected raw credential and overrides a persisted protection choice. A selected protected route fails closed before any credential-bearing spawn when the raw key cannot be contained or the proxy cannot start; there is no automatic downgrade to raw.
- `cwd` — string. Working directory (ignored with isolate; sandboxed under MCP)
- `timeout` — number. Seconds before the engine is killed (default 1500 over MCP)

### `triss_coder_status`

Show coding-agent setup: canonical provider credential readiness, default engine, engine versions/install state, configured engine files, and active isolation worktrees.

### `triss_coder_result_list`

### `triss_coder_result_clean`

Remove ONLY a validated retained result artifact by its run-id (run-<32 lowercase hex>). Never removes a persistent session selected by a slug.

Input properties:

- `run_id` — string (required). run-id of the retained result to remove
